title: Bar and column charts: ordering and a baseline at zero

videos.script: A bar chart is the most common chart in any office. It is also the one most often drawn wrong. {{common}} Here are two columns. Northeast and South, Horta's orders last year. On the left, Northeast is a little taller. On the right, it is six times taller. {{two}} The numbers are the same. Only the axis moved. On the right, it starts at thirty-four thousand instead of zero. {{axis}} A bar says its number with its length. Cut off the bottom of the bar, and the length says something else. {{length}} That is the one rule of bar charts that is not a matter of style. The baseline is zero. {{rule}} The rest of this lesson is about choices that are matters of judgement. Bars or columns. What order to put them in. When to group them and when to stack them. {{choices}} Each choice changes which comparison the reader makes first. By the end, you will choose on purpose. {{purpose}}
